newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse changes Thermo King plans.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse changes Thermo King plans.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp said Wednesday that in a change to its plans to separate its media and industrial businesses, the Thermo King refrigerated transport group will remain with the media division, along with existing Westinghouse pension and post-retirement benefit obligations.
The change does not alter the timing of the separation, which is scheduled for this autumn, the company said.

"By retaining Thermo King (in the parent company media business), we have greater flexibility to apply its strong cash flow to reduce liabilities, and also to maintain several attractive options to optimize the value of Thermo King," said Westinghouse Chief Executive Michael Jordan.
Westinghouse said the change would make the industrial business eligible for better financing.
Retaining pension and other post-retirement benefit obligations at the media business, to be named CBS Corp, will mean cash savings for the industrial business, it said.
For the industrial business, these savings will outweigh the lost cash flow contribution from Thermo King, Westinghouse said.

Under Westinghouse's original separation plan, existing pension and other post-retirement benefit obligations were to be transferred to the industrial business. Also, Thermo King was to be part of the industrial group, and a portion of Thermo King was to be spun off in a public offering.
Westinghouse said today it would consider various options to enhance Thermo King's value to shareholders, including a sale, public offering or spin-off to shareholders.
If Thermo King is sold, the company's net tax operating loss carryforward would be used to shelter the gain on disposition, Westinghouse said.
